key_insight: Interfacial suboxide chemistry couples tensile deformation to bond weakening in oxidized silicon nanowires, while crystallographic facet orientation shapes the electronic response to strain.
engineering_relevance: Controlling interface chemistry and facet orientation could help tune strain-dependent electronic behavior while managing localized mechanical failure in silicon nanowire devices.
method: Simulate dry thermal oxidation with reactive force field molecular dynamics.
Track interfacial bond evolution and stress gradients under tensile strain.
Use density functional theory on facet-specific models to probe electronic response.
evidence_signal: Simulations show elongated, lower-bond-order interfacial Si–Si bonds associated with partial oxidation, localized stress and preferential rupture, alongside facet-dependent electronic responses in first-principles calculations.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational findings without experimental validation or quantitative device-performance benchmarks.
paper_title: Strain-Induced Interfacial Bond Evolution and Facet-dependent Strain Response of Electronic Properties in Oxidized Silicon Nanowires
